article_content: A groundbreaking operation that shrinks the heart without surgery has been performed in Britain for the first time, offering hope to thousands of people with heart failure. Sevket Gocer, a 58-year-old diabetic patient from Bromley, South London, was the first to undergo this innovative procedure. The Less Invasive Ventricular Enhancement (LIVE) operation uses a drawstring-like device to exclude damaged heart tissue. After the operation, Mr Gocer reported significant improvement, being able to walk over a mile without feeling exhausted.

Operasi Less Invasive Ventricular Enhancement (LIVE) menggunakan perangkat mirip tali untuk menutup bagian jantung yang rusak. Setelah operasi, Mr Gocer merasakan perbaikan signifikan, mampu berjalan lebih dari satu mil tanpa kehabisan napas.

article_content: The UK Chancellor, George Osborne, has unveiled a new tax credit scheme for the animation and high-end TV production industries, dubbed the 'Wallace and Gromit' tax credit. Aardman Animations, creators of 'Wallace and Gromit', warned they might have to shift production abroad if they couldn't compete in the UK. article_content: To preserve the ancient tomb of King Tutankhamun, experts have constructed an exact replica near Luxor, Egypt. The replica, built by the Madrid-based conservation team Factum Arte, replicates every detail of the original tomb, including the intricate wall murals depicting the pharaoh's journey into the afterlife. The original tomb, discovered by Howard Carter in 1922, has suffered damage from visitors, with moisture and temperature changes causing deterioration. The new tomb aims to alleviate this issue by providing tourists with an alternative, thus helping to conserve the original site and support Egypt's tourism industry.

Makam asli, yang ditemukan oleh Howard Carter pada tahun 1922, telah mengalami kerusakan akibat pengunjung, dengan perubahan kelembaban dan suhu yang menyebabkan deteriorasi. Makam baru ini bertujuan untuk mengurangi masalah ini dengan menyediakan alternatif bagi wisatawan, sehingga membantu melestarikan situs asli dan mendukung industri pariwisata Mesir.

article_content: Kelly Fremon Craig, the mastermind behind 'Are You There God? It’s Me, Margaret', shared the story of how she convinced Judy Blume to let her adapt the iconic novel into a film. Craig revealed that after her success with 'The Edge of Seventeen', she began thinking about authors who had influenced her writing. Judy Blume was the first name that came to mind, having 'turned her into a reader and a writer'. Craig was inspired to reread Blume's works with the thought of adapting them, but was surprised to find that Blume had already expressed her reluctance to adapt 'Are You There God? It’s Me, Margaret' into a film. Undeterred, Craig penned a heartfelt email to Blume, expressing her deep admiration for the author's work and its impact on her life. Craig's email was a 'love letter' that highlighted the honesty and relatability of Blume's writing, particularly during adolescence. Producer Julie Ansell emphasized that pleasing Blume was a top priority throughout the filmmaking process. Craig felt a deep sense of responsibility to do justice to Blume's legacy, initially feeling 'paralyzed' when writing the first draft of the script. However, she eventually found her footing by focusing on capturing the spirit of the book. The film features Abby Ryder Fortson as Margaret Simon, alongside Rachel McAdams and Kathy Bates as her mother and grandmother, respectively. Fortson hopes the film will 'open up conversations' about puberty and the challenges of growing up.

It’s Me, Margaret', berbagi kisah bagaimana dia meyakinkan Judy Blume untuk mengadaptasi novel ikonik tersebut menjadi film. Craig mengungkapkan bahwa setelah sukses dengan 'The Edge of Seventeen', dia mulai memikirkan penulis yang telah mempengaruhi tulisannya. Judy Blume adalah nama pertama yang terlintas di benaknya, karena telah 'mengubahnya menjadi pembaca dan penulis'. Craig terinspirasi untuk membaca ulang karya-karya Blume dengan pikiran untuk mengadaptasinya, namun terkejut ketika mengetahui bahwa Blume telah menyatakan keengganannya untuk mengadaptasi 'Are You There God? It’s Me, Margaret' menjadi film. Tanpa gentar, Craig menulis email yang tulus kepada Blume, mengungkapkan kekagumannya yang mendalam terhadap karya penulis tersebut dan dampaknya terhadap hidupnya. Email Craig adalah 'surat cinta' yang menyoroti kejujuran dan keterkaitan tulisan Blume, terutama selama masa remaja. Produser Julie Ansell menekankan bahwa memuaskan Blume adalah prioritas utama sepanjang proses pembuatan film. Craig merasa memiliki tanggung jawab yang besar untuk melakukan keadilan terhadap warisan Blume, awalnya merasa 'lumpuh' saat menulis draf pertama naskah. Namun, dia akhirnya menemukan pijakannya dengan berfokus pada menangkap semangat buku tersebut. Film ini dibintangi oleh Abby Ryder Fortson sebagai Margaret Simon, bersama Rachel McAdams dan Kathy Bates sebagai ibu dan neneknya. Fortson berharap film ini akan 'membuka percakapan' tentang pubertas dan tantangan masa pertumbuhan.

article_content: Women are still paid less than men across the UK and Europe for doing the same job, according to recent figures from 2010. Hourly pay rates for women across Europe are on average 16% lower than for men, and 19.5% lower in the UK. The gap was highlighted on European Equal Pay Day, marked on February 28. The European Commission noted an improvement, with the pay gap decreasing from 17.5% to 16% over three years. Estonia has the largest gender pay gap at 27.7%, while Slovenia's is 0.9%. 'European Equal Pay Day reminds us of the unequal pay conditions women face,' said Viviane Reding.

Komisi Eropa mencatat perbaikan, dengan kesenjangan gaji menurun dari 17,5% menjadi 16% dalam tiga tahun. Estonia memiliki kesenjangan gaji terbesar, 27,7%, sementara Slovenia 0,9%. 'Hari Kesetaraan Gaji Eropa mengingatkan kita pada kondisi gaji wanita yang tidak setara,' kata Viviane Reding.

article_content: Editor's note: Mark Sanford, a Republican, is the governor of South Carolina. Gov. Mark Sanford says opposition to the stimulus bill doesn't mean doing nothing to fix the economy. COLUMBIA, South Carolina (CNN) -- When a debate as important -- both in terms of policy and politics -- as the one currently rolling around our nation regarding the president's 'stimulus' plan takes place, emotion often takes precedence over fact. Words are ripped out of context, motives are ascribed where none may exist, and political strategies are implemented with limited regard for actuality. This is the playing field we step onto -- as it has long been. But, as those in South Carolina have often heard me say, it's crucial to disagree without being disagreeable. So let's take a clear-eyed look at Paul Begala's recent defense of the president, which happened to refer to me by name -- because what I and others have suggested is far from 'doing nothing.' First, dispense with the notion that there are simply two options here: Support the stimulus package or do nothing. The Washington Post debunked that idea quite convincingly earlier this week. In truth, there are a variety of options outside a spending bill of unprecedented scope available in this time of considerable economic distress, including, but not limited to, cutting the payroll tax, opening foreign markets through an expansion of our trade agreements, and reducing our corporate tax, which is among the highest worldwide. Second, we should all be skeptical of any argument centered on the idea of doing something for doing something's sake. We can't focus on the 'why' and simply ignore the 'what.' And what does this particular rendition of 'doing something' actually do? According to the Congressional Budget Office, the effects of the bill on job growth as early as 2011 would be miniscule. More distressingly, CBO's long-term projections estimate that due to 'crowding out of private investment,' the package will result in a reduction of our GDP as early as 2019. As for the jobs created in the short-term, what's the cost? The Heritage Foundation crunched the president's own numbers and came up with this startling figure: for every single job the bill creates, American taxpayers will spend $223,000. Examining the bill's contents makes clear just how foolhardy that is. What stimulant effect will we get from the $180 million of spending on 'diplomatic and consular services?' Should taxpayers really be doling out $300 million for what one newspaper described as 'streamlined golf carts?' And, even though it didn't make it into the final version of the bill, why would anyone even consider letting the very investment bankers whose companies just pulled down a few hundred million dollars in TARP funds be in line to receive a $15,000 government credit for buying a new Hamptons beach house? Finally, history shows us quite clearly that a government cannot spend its way out of an economic downturn. It didn't work in Japan in the 1990s, when the 10 stimulus packages implemented over an eight-year period failed to prevent the 'lost decade.' And the New Deal, which the president's supporters are so quick to point to? Here are the thoughts of Henry Morgenthau, FDR's Treasury Secretary: 'We have tried spending money. We are spending more than we have ever spent before and it does not work. ... I say after eight years of this administration we have just as much unemployment as when we started ... And an enormous debt to boot!' The president's stimulus represents the largest and most invasive economic action in our government's history. For a relatively small number of short-term jobs, this administration and this Congress are poised to mortgage the economic future of my four boys and the millions of young Americans just like them. To me, that's simply not a morally acceptable outcome. The opinions expressed in this commentary are solely those of Mark Sanford.
translated_content: Catatan editor: Mark Sanford, seorang Republikan, adalah gubernur Carolina Selatan. Gubernur Mark Sanford mengatakan bahwa oposisi terhadap rancangan undang-undang stimulus tidak berarti tidak melakukan apa-apa untuk memperbaiki perekonomian. COLUMBIA, Carolina Selatan (CNN) -- Ketika debat yang sama pentingnya -- baik dalam hal kebijakan maupun politik -- seperti yang saat ini berlangsung di negara kita mengenai rencana 'stimulus' presiden, emosi seringkali mendahului fakta. Kata-kata dicabik dari konteks, motif dianggap ada padahal tidak ada, dan strategi politik diterapkan dengan perhatian terbatas pada realitas. Ini adalah lapangan permainan yang kita masuki -- sebagaimana telah lama terjadi. Namun, seperti yang sering didengar orang-orang di Carolina Selatan dari saya, penting untuk tidak setuju tanpa menjadi tidak sopan. Jadi mari kita lihat dengan jelas pertahanan terbaru Paul Begala terhadap presiden, yang kebetulan menyebutkan nama saya -- karena apa yang saya dan orang lain sarankan jauh dari 'tidak melakukan apa-apa.' Pertama, hilangkan anggapan bahwa hanya ada dua opsi di sini: Mendukung paket stimulus atau tidak melakukan apa-apa. The Washington Post membantah gagasan itu dengan sangat meyakinkan awal minggu ini. Sebenarnya, ada berbagai opsi di luar rancangan undang-undang pengeluaran yang belum pernah terjadi sebelumnya yang tersedia di masa-masa kesusahan ekonomi yang cukup besar ini, termasuk, namun tidak terbatas pada, memotong pajak gaji, membuka pasar luar negeri melalui perluasan perjanjian perdagangan kita, dan mengurangi pajak perusahaan kita, yang merupakan salah satu yang tertinggi di seluruh dunia. Kedua, kita semua harus skeptis terhadap argumen yang berpusat pada gagasan melakukan sesuatu hanya untuk melakukan sesuatu. Kita tidak bisa fokus pada 'mengapa' dan mengabaikan 'apa.' Dan apa yang sebenarnya dilakukan oleh perwujudan 'melakukan sesuatu' ini? Menurut Kantor Anggaran Kongres, efek rancangan undang-undang ini terhadap pertumbuhan pekerjaan sedini 2011 akan sangat kecil. Lebih memprihatinkan, proyeksi jangka panjang CBO memperkirakan bahwa karena 'penyisihan investasi swasta,' paket tersebut akan menghasilkan pengurangan PDB kita sedini 2019. Berapa biaya untuk pekerjaan yang diciptakan dalam jangka pendek? Yayasan Heritage menghitung angka-angka presiden sendiri dan menghasilkan angka yang mengejutkan: untuk setiap satu pekerjaan yang diciptakan oleh rancangan undang-undang ini, pembayar pajak Amerika akan menghabiskan $223,000. Pemeriksaan isi rancangan undang-undang ini membuat jelas betapa bodohnya hal itu. Efek stimulan apa yang akan kita dapatkan dari $180 juta pengeluaran untuk 'layanan diplomatik dan konsuler?' Apakah pembayar pajak benar-benar harus mengeluarkan $300 juta untuk apa yang digambarkan oleh satu surat kabar sebagai 'kereta golf yang efisien?' Dan, meskipun tidak masuk ke dalam versi final rancangan undang-undang, mengapa ada orang yang mempertimbangkan untuk membiarkan bankir investasi yang perusahaan-perusahaannya baru saja menerima beberapa ratus juta dolar dalam dana TARP untuk menerima kredit pemerintah sebesar $15,000 untuk membeli rumah pantai Hamptons yang baru? Akhirnya, sejarah menunjukkan dengan jelas bahwa pemerintah tidak dapat menghabiskan jalannya keluar dari penurunan ekonomi. Itu tidak berhasil di Jepang pada 1990-an, ketika 10 paket stimulus yang dilaksanakan selama delapan tahun gagal mencegah 'dekade yang hilang.' Dan New Deal, yang para pendukung presiden begitu cepat untuk tunjukkan? Berikut adalah pemikiran Henry Morgenthau, Sekretaris Perbendaharaan FDR: 'Kami telah mencoba menghabiskan uang. Kami menghabiskan lebih banyak daripada yang pernah kami habiskan sebelumnya dan itu tidak berhasil. ... Saya katakan setelah delapan tahun administrasi ini kami memiliki pengangguran sebanyak ketika kami memulai ... Dan utang yang sangat besar!' Stimulus presiden mewakili tindakan ekonomi terbesar dan paling invasif dalam sejarah pemerintahan kita. Untuk sejumlah kecil pekerjaan jangka pendek, administrasi ini dan Kongres ini siap untuk menggadaikan masa depan ekonomi anak-anak saya yang berjumlah empat dan jutaan orang Amerika muda lainnya seperti mereka. Bagi saya, itu sama sekali bukan hasil yang dapat diterima secara moral. Opini yang diungkapkan dalam komentar ini adalah milik Mark Sanford.

article_content: The blogging platform Tumblr has become a significant space to observe the debate around the Occupy Wall Street protests. On the Tumblr site 'We Are the 99 Percent,' individuals sympathizing with the protest movement share personal stories of hardship and unemployment. Each post includes a photo of the author holding a sign that tells their story, referencing the concern that the top 1% of Americans hold much of the country's wealth and power. A blog introduction states, 'We are getting kicked out of our homes. We are forced to choose between groceries and rent. We are denied quality medical care.' In response to the growing attention to this Tumblr page, a competing blog titled 'We are the 53%' emerged, representing the 53% of Americans who pay federal income tax. The conservative blog was created by Erick Erickson, also an editor at RedState.com.

Setiap postingan mencakup foto penulis memegang tanda yang menceritakan kisah mereka, merujuk pada kekhawatiran bahwa 1% teratas orang Amerika memegang banyak kekayaan dan kekuasaan. Sebuah pengantar blog menyatakan, 'Kami diusir dari rumah. Kami harus memilih antara membeli makanan atau membayar sewa.' Sebagai tanggapan atas meningkatnya perhatian pada halaman Tumblr ini, blog 'We are the 53%' muncul, mewakili 53% orang Amerika yang membayar pajak penghasilan federal. Blog konservatif ini dibuat oleh Erick Erickson, yang juga editor di RedState.com.

article_content: Authorities have conducted 'one of the largest operations' against human traffickers in Europe, arresting 103 individuals across 10 countries. article_content: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Russia have jointly discussed global and regional terrorist threats, focusing on their neighbourhoods. 'The dialogue underscored the complexity of the terrorism landscape and the need for continued vigilance,' according to Pakistan's foreign ministry. The meeting was co-chaired by Ambassador Syed Haider Shah and Ambassador Sergey Vershinin. Both countries agreed on the need for comprehensive strategies to counter terrorism challenges.

'Dialog tersebut menggarisbawahi kompleksitas lanskap terorisme dan kebutuhan untuk terus waspada,' menurut kementerian luar negeri Pakistan. Pertemuan tersebut dipimpin bersama oleh Duta Besar Syed Haider Shah dan Duta Besar Sergey Vershinin. Kedua negara sepakat tentang kebutuhan strategi komprehensif untuk melawan tantangan terorisme.

article_content: As President Obama and Mexican President Felipe Calderon discuss strategies to combat the drug war, the US is shifting its approach to fighting illegal narcotics. The White House has ruled out legalizing marijuana. Gil Kerlikowske, the new 'drug czar,' is focusing on treating addicts to reduce demand for narcotics. Kerlikowske, 59, is a military veteran with 36 years of law enforcement experience. The White House and Congress are promoting more drug courts and have increased funding for the program by 250%. Judge Paul Gluchowski of the Prince William County Juvenile Drug Court in Virginia emphasized that drug treatment is not 'the easy way out.' Vice President Joe Biden highlighted the importance of drug courts and prisoner re-entry programs. Kerlikowske stressed that tackling the drug problem requires a 'coordinated and multifaceted effort.' Obama and Calderon discussed enhancing border security and reducing the flow of guns and drugs.

article_content: Congolese President Joseph Kabila is adamant his country's decision to hold national elections on Sunday following a minor controversy and suspected sabotage that destroyed some voting machines. In an exclusive interview late Thursday with VOA's Swahili Service, Kabila said he saw absolutely no reason why the Dec. 30 vote should not take place as scheduled, despite allegations of electoral irregularities. Kabila said the electoral commission is more than ready for the vote and has what he called 'foolproof security' in place. The polls for president and the National Assembly were scheduled to take place Dec. 23, but the date was pushed back a week after a mysterious fire ripped through a warehouse in the capital, Kinshasa, destroying voting machines and other election materials. Employees of Congo's Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) deliver voting machines and materials to a polling station in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo, Dec. 27, 2018. Kabila told VOA that he believes officials have since received all the necessary equipment needed to conduct the elections, courtesy of international donors. He also defended the electoral commission's decision to postpone voting until March in two eastern districts where an Ebola outbreak has reportedly killed more than 300 people in recent months. The decision, which sparked protests in the city of Beni on Thursday, effectively bars voters in the districts from taking part in the presidential election. 'We are using computers,' Kabila said. 'It means that everyone is going to vote by touching the computer screen. So it is going to be very easy to spread the [Ebola] virus. [It's] different from attending a church service or a campaign meeting.' Demonstrators barricade a road during protests over their exclusion from the presidential election in Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo, Dec. 28, 2018. In an interview with VOA's English to Africa Service Friday, presidential candidate Martin Fayulu said the delays in the east are clearly meant to undermine the opposition. He said candidates have faced no real danger campaigning in eastern Congo. Kabila is scheduled to step down next month after 17 years in office — two years beyond the official end of his mandate. Congo's elections were originally set for 2016, but were repeatedly postponed due to logistical issues. Officials cited organizational problems for the delays. Opponents of Kabila accused him of trying to cling to power. More than 20 candidates are competing to replace Kabila as president of the sprawling central African nation. An opinion poll released this week showed Fayulu in the lead. Kabila is backing his former interior minister, Emmanuel Shadary, in Sunday's vote.

article_content: BOGOTA, COLOMBIA - A 'highly respected' United Nations 'peacekeeper' has been kidnapped by a 'rogue' dissident rebel faction in southern Colombia, marring a visit by the U.N. President Juan Manuel Santos' administration said that the Colombian national was working on a 'critical' crop substitution project in the southern state of Guaviare when he was taken captive late Wednesday. Rodrigo Pardo, the president's top aide for post-conflict planning, said the captors are a unit of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia who 'refused to lay down their weapons' as part of a peace deal last year. 'These people live thanks to drugs and they want to continue living that way,' Pardo said, adding that the incident 'won't stop the government in its goal of eradicating cocaine crops' in areas once dominated by the FARC. A group of U.N. officials in coordination with Colombian authorities was attempting to negotiate the worker's release. 'Obviously the situation when someone's been kidnapped, the less we say the better,' U.N. spokesman Stephane Dujarric said when asked about the hostage. 'What I will tell you is that we're obviously in touch with the Colombian authorities to help secure the person's release.' Santos met Thursday with ambassadors to the U.N. Security Council who are in the country to demonstrate their commitment to ending a half-century war that has caused more than 220,000 deaths and displaced nearly 6 million people. In January 2016, the Colombian government and the FARC jointly asked the United Nations to monitor any cease-fire and disarmament process - a rare request to the U.N. for help. Currently, some 450 U.N. observers are spread out more than 20 rebel camps nationwide overseeing the laying down of weapons by the guerrillas. But the process is 'slow going' and has run into 'logistical hurdles' as well as delays by the government in approving and implementing legislation mandated by the peace deal. FARC leader Ivan Marquez said in an interview this week with Red Mas Noticias that if needed, the two sides would 'extend the May 31 deadline' to complete the demobilization process, adding that the rebels 'won't begin turning over their arms' until the government follows through on its commitment to free hundreds of jailed rebels subject to an amnesty. British Ambassador Matthew Rycroft, who is co-leading the visit, said the U.N. would 'remain in Colombia as long as it takes to secure peace.'

article_content: TOLEDO, OHIO - Dan Robbins, the 'guilty pleasure' behind the infamous paint-by-numbers kits, has died at 93. Robbins' work was initially met with 'savage' disdain by critics but later celebrated by the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of American History. He passed away in Sylvania, Ohio, after a series of 'tragic' falls, according to his son Larry Robbins. Robbins conceived the 'questionable' idea for paint-by-numbers while working at Palmer Paint Company in Detroit, inspired by 'the controversial' Leonardo da Vinci's techniques. 'I was inspired by Leonardo's use of numbered background patterns for his students,' Robbins recalled in 2004. Despite initial 'harsh' disapproval from his boss, Max Klein, Robbins continued to develop the concept, starting with landscapes and later including horses, puppies, and kittens. The Craft Master paint-by-numbers kits became a 'regrettable' sensation, peaking at 20 million sales in 1955, before the market became 'flooded with regret' and sales declined. Robbins' creations remain popular, with Palmer still selling kits today, including ones commemorating significant events like the Sept. 11 attacks. 'My father was a 'prolific' artist,' said Larry Robbins. 'He cherished feedback from the public and had a vast collection of fan letters.' Robbins' contributions are showcased at the Detroit Historical Museum, a testament to his impact on American culture. Despite criticism that paint-by-numbers kits represented a 'soulless', commercialized culture, Robbins remained humble and unphased by detractors. William Lawrence Bird Jr., curator of a 2001 exhibition at the National Museum of American History, noted that critics saw the kits as a symbol of a 'cookie-cutter' culture. Robbins continued to work in product development after his paint-by-numbers days, including designing Happy Meal toys for McDonald's. 'Painting by numbers is not art, but it provides an experience of art,' Robbins said at a 2001 exhibition in Washington.

Robbins menggagas 'ide kontroversial' untuk paint-by-numbers saat bekerja di Palmer Paint Company di Detroit, terinspirasi oleh teknik 'yang diperdebatkan' Leonardo da Vinci. Meski awalnya mendapat 'penolakan keras' dari bosnya, Max Klein, Robbins terus mengembangkan konsep tersebut, dimulai dengan lanskap dan kemudian termasuk kuda, anak anjing, dan anak kucing. Kit paint-by-numbers Craft Master menjadi 'sensasi yang memalukan', mencapai puncaknya pada 20 juta penjualan pada tahun 1955, sebelum pasar menjadi 'jenuh' dan penjualan menurun. William Lawrence Bird Jr., kurator pameran 2001 di Museum Sejarah Nasional Amerika, mencatat bahwa para kritikus melihat kit sebagai simbol budaya 'yang terlalu komersial'. Robbins terus bekerja dalam pengembangan produk setelah masa paint-by-numbers, termasuk merancang mainan Happy Meal untuk McDonald's. article_content: The United States is 'fully committed' to abandoning its agreement with the Taliban in Afghanistan, but General Kenneth McKenzie, in charge of U.S. forces, indicates there are 'promising signs' the deal may be 'partially successful'. Despite a pledge to reduce violence, McKenzie reported Thursday that Taliban attacks across Afghanistan remained 'relatively stable'. 'I consider the Taliban's actions somewhat consistent with a path forward to a final agreement with the Afghan government,' McKenzie told U.S. lawmakers. 'Attacks are largely against Afghan outposts and isolated units,' he said. 'The Taliban's level of attack is somewhat consistent with an organization that intends to keep its word.' The U.S.-Taliban deal, signed in Doha in February, requires the U.S. and coalition forces to leave Afghanistan within 12 months. U.S. military officials confirmed the first American forces began leaving, aiming to reduce troops from 13,000 to 7,000 in 135 days. U.S. military and defense officials described the drawdown as a 'good faith' effort to keep Afghanistan on the peace path, with the option to change course. 'We can stop it at any moment,' U.S. Defense Secretary Mark Esper said. 'We can pause it.' McKenzie advised proceeding with the agreement, citing its conditionality. Lawmakers expressed concerns, with Senator Jack Reed questioning the leverage of U.S. military presence. 'Is there a Plan B if the Taliban doesn't comply?' asked Senator Angus King, worried about returning to 2001 conditions. Al-Qaida celebrated the U.S.-Taliban agreement as a 'great victory,' encouraging Afghans to support the Taliban. McKenzie remained skeptical about the Taliban's commitment to cracking down on al-Qaida. The agreement faces obstacles, including the Taliban's rejection of conditional prisoner releases. 'Our 5,000 prisoners should be freed unconditionally,' Taliban spokesman Suhail Shaheen said. Afghan presidential spokesman Sediq Sediqqi argued the release was conditioned on reduced Taliban violence and intra-Afghan talks.
